summary: Tested the licence rest feature (Madrid libranzas) end to end. Backend: 21/21 pytest passed (15 new API tests plus the 6 existing unit tests). Covered: /license-rest/me (unknown licence, and three licences compared against the pure rules on the container date Mon 2026-11-02, which is also a holiday); holidays list/add/disable/404/422/non-admin 401-403/sync; the disabled flag surviving a re-sync; client driver-availability (no auth, unknown licence, weekly rest, out of shift, in shift, ISO time with a Z suffix); create_ride with send_to_pool (scheduled >12h and ASAP become open/preferred=false), the default scheduled >12h ride staying assigned, and prefer_my_driver keeping its 30-min window. Frontend (mobile 390x844): the Calle banner shows 'Hoy libras / Libras hasta mañana a las 06:00 (libranza semanal)' at the top of the tab. The Admin HolidaysAdmin add, disable (row greyed, trash icon hidden), invalid-date message and sync all work. In the client Emisora app, the toggle shows the availability text, submitting opens the unavailable modal, 'Enviar a todos' created an open ride and 'Enviar igualmente' created an assigned ride with preferred=true and a 30-min window (checked in the DB).

minor.issue: The driver cannot clear their licence: an empty string fails the isdigit() check and returns 400.
The 422 message reads 'Value error, Fecha inválida (AAAA-MM-DD)' (Pydantic prefix) and the UI shows it as-is. @validator is deprecated in Pydantic v2.
The message is built from the driver-facing label, so the client reads 'Tu taxista tiene libranza semanal a esa hora (libras hasta mañana a las 06:00)'. 'libras' should be 'libra'.

A scheduled ride >12h ahead with the trusted-driver toggle off still becomes exclusive (dispatch_scope=assigned) to the associated driver. No availability check or warning is made, even if the driver rests at that time.

ui_bugs.issue: The address-suggestion dropdown (it suggested non-Madrid places like 'Solarstraße, Eberstalzell') stays open behind the modal.
If the client submits before the availability fetch finishes (driverAvail is null), no modal appears and the ride goes straight to the trusted driver.

issues: HolidaysAdmin (14+ rows) sits above the admin stats and pushes them far down; consider making it collapsible.
A disabled holiday can only be re-enabled by re-adding the same date; there is no re-enable button.
The banner only refreshes every 60s, so a licence just saved in the profile is not reflected immediately.

action_items: Fix the client-facing availability message wording ('libra hasta ...' instead of 'libras hasta ...').
Decide whether scheduled >12h rides (auto-exclusive to the associated driver) should also check availability and warn the client.
Strip the 'Value error, ' prefix from validation messages in HolidaysAdmin, or raise HTTPException 400.
Optional: allow clearing the licence, close address suggestions before opening the modal, make HolidaysAdmin collapsible.
critical_code_review_comments: EmisoraClient scheduledIso uses the device's local timezone (new Date(`${d}T${t}:00`)); this is fine for Madrid users but wrong if the device timezone differs.
rides.py line 913: 'associated_driver_id if dispatch_scope == "assigned" else associated_driver_id' has identical branches (dead conditional).
sync_madrid_calendar overwrites source/name of manually added dates that are also in the CSV (harmless).
